subject: Coffee & Tea
title: The Chaiwala: India's Tea Vendors
description: A fast breakdown of The Chaiwala: India's Tea Vendors for builders.

hook.text: Chaiwalas (tea vendors) operate on nearly every street corner in India. There are an estimated 5 million of them.

buildup.text: A chaiwala works from a simple stall—a gas burner, a pot, glasses, and a small counter. Startup costs are minimal.

discovery.text: A cup from a chaiwala costs 10–20 rupees (about $0.12–$0.25). It's the most democratic beverage in Indian society.

twist.text: India's PM Modi began as a chaiwala at his father's tea stall—a backstory that became powerful campaign gold.

climax.text: Chaiwalas are community anchors. Morning tea at the corner stall is where neighbors meet, gossip, and begin each day.

punchline.text: Five million stalls, 12-cent cups, one nation glued together by chai.

quiz.question: How many chaiwalas (tea vendors) operate in India?

details.summary: Chaiwalas are mobile and roadside tea vendors found on nearly every street corner in India. They brew chai in huge kettles, serve it in small clay or glass cups, and sell it for a few rupees.
details.whyItMatters: Chaiwalas are the backbone of Indian tea culture and micro-entrepreneurship. They serve millions daily and provide essential social gathering points in every neighborhood.
takeaways: Chaiwalas are roadside tea vendors found across all of India
They serve chai in small cups for just a few rupees
They provide essential social gathering points in communities

faq.question: How much does a cup of chai cost from a chaiwala?
faq.answer: A standard cup costs 10 to 20 rupees, roughly 10 to 25 US cents, making it one of the most affordable prepared beverages in the world. Some premium chaiwalas charge more for special blends. The ultra-low price makes chai accessible to virtually everyone in India.

faq.question: Can being a chaiwala lead to success?
faq.answer: India's current Prime Minister Narendra Modi famously worked as a chaiwala in his youth. Many successful restaurant and food business owners started as chai vendors. While most chaiwalas earn modest incomes, the profession offers an entry point to entrepreneurship with very low startup costs.
